messages:
deploy-bot: Preflight failure: chart=analytics-v7.0 attempted CRD upgrade for AnalyticsJob.crds.redwood.ai from v1alpha1 to v1beta1 in 2/8 canary namespaces; api validation errors observed. severity=blocker for automatic promote. cmd: `kubectl -n prod get crd analyticsjobs.crds.redwood.ai -o yaml`
eric: saw the validationErrors in canary: `unknown field: spec.executionOptions.maxRetries` when CRD version bumped. The new CRD schema added stricter validation.
maya: where did the CRD change come from? promoted chart 7.0 includes crds/analyticsjob.crd.yaml v1beta1. The cluster currently has v1alpha1 installed by earlier deployment.
lina: options: 1) abort promotion and keep current CRD, 2) promote but set `--set crds.install=false` and leave manual CRD rollout to infra, 3) rollforward CRD now with a careful staged apply and migration job. Given business need for feature in 7.0, could we do controlled rollforward?
\meric: I think controlled rollforward is doable but needs a migration runbook. Plan outline: a) apply CRD using server-side apply to allow structural changes: `kubectl apply -f crds/analyticsjob.v1beta1.yaml --server-side=true`; b) run schema migration job in canary namespace to check object conversions; c) if green, run cluster-wide migration and then promote chart.
maya: runbook sketch and commands:```bash
# 1) dry-run apply with server-side
kubectl apply -f crds/analyticsjob.v1beta1.yaml --server-side=true --dry-run=client
# 2) apply to a canary namespace
kubectl -n prod-canary apply -f crds/analyticsjob.v1beta1.yaml --server-side=true
# 3) run conversion job
kubectl -n prod-canary create job convert-analyticsjob-v1beta1 --image=redwood/tools:latest -- /convert --target-version v1beta1
# 4) if canary conversion OK, apply cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f crds/analyticsjob.v1beta1.yaml --server-side=true
# 5) promote chart after CRD is installed
helm upgrade analytics-release charts/analytics --namespace prod --version 7.0.0 --reuse-values --set imagePromotion.meta=crd-rollforward-2026-07-12
```
eric: rollback surface: if CRD conversion breaks, we can't rollback CRD easily; mitigation is to gate the CRD upgrade behind manual approval and keep previous controller running while conversion job runs. If conversion fails, we should stop and restore objects from backups. Helm rollback for the chart still possible but CRD changes persist.
lina: we need signoff from infra and DB (since jobs touch storage). Also add watch for creation failures and controller crashloops. Requesting infra oncall watch for 60m. @oncall-bot can you add a 60m watch for analytics-controller restarts? :eyes:
release-manager: timeline: change window still open for 2h. This is higher-risk than a pin; prefer conservative approach. Propose hybrid: perform CRD server-side apply only to a single canary namespace now, run conversion job and validate, keep main promotion paused. If canary passes within 30m, escalate to full cluster apply and promote. Document everything in release notes and the audit.
maya: acknowledged. I'll prepare the conversion job image and RBAC. Creating ticket RD-6340 to track CRD rollforward and migration runbook.
eric: running canary CRD apply now (dry-run passed). will post conversion job logs to thread.
release-manager: decision: proceed with staged CRD rollforward starting in a canary namespace; main chart promotion paused until conversion validated. Add short release-note: "CRD schema upgrade staged in canary; chart promo deferred pending conversion validation. Follow-up: scheduled cluster CRD apply and migration if canary passes." Assign RD-6340 to @maya and @eric.
eric: applied to prod-canary at 4005002505. conversion job started. Logs show initial conversions ok for 12/12 objects; one object failed due to unknown field and will be reconciled by ops.
maya: will fix conversion tool to drop deprecated field and re-run. re-run scheduled immediately.
release-manager: keep thread open until canary conversion validated or timeout. If canary green by 4005002780 we'll proceed cluster-wide and then promote. Otherwise rollback to step of leaving chart at previous version. :rocket:
